name: Visibility – Lightweight SEO, AEO and GEO for Search and AI
author: Fernando Tellado

sections.description:
Visibility is the SEO essentials in one light plugin: meta tags, canonical URLs, Open Graph, schema, robots rules, redirects, a robots.txt editor, llms.txt, Markdown for AI agents and control of the native XML sitemap, in about 690 KB.

  • Free, all of it. No Pro version, no upsell banners, no account.
  • No tracking. Nothing phones home.
  • Light. Built on WordPress core APIs, with no database tables of its own and no cron jobs.
  • Easy to switch to. One-click import from Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, The SEO Framework, Slim SEO and SureRank.
  • Ready for AI search (AEO and GEO). Clean metadata, llms.txt and a Markdown version of every page, for ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and other AI assistants to read and cite.

Four modules, switch on only what you need

Discover: meta tags, schema and AI discovery

  • Meta title and meta description, with templates and per-post and per-term overrides.
  • Canonical URLs on entries and on every listing.
  • Open Graph and Twitter Cards.
  • JSON-LD schema: Article, BreadcrumbList, Person, ProfilePage, FAQPage and Site Identity (Organization, LocalBusiness or Person). Choose the type per content type, or None to leave it to another plugin.
  • What each entry is about, in its own Schema tab: a local business, a product, a service, an event, a recipe, a book, a course, a job posting, a how-to and ten more types, with an optional review. A template per content type fills it from the entry, a custom field or the Site Identity, and it is written only with what Google requires.
  • Author details (job title, topics and credentials), shown with the Author details block or the [visibility_author_details] shortcode. Each author can pick a page as their profile page.
  • AI discovery: llms.txt, llms-full.txt, a Markdown version of each page and a robots.txt editor with AI crawler rules.
  • Respect nosnippet: content set to nosnippet stays out of the llms.txt summaries, llms-full.txt, Markdown and FAQPage.
  • A filter for content that has not been updated in a while.

Indexing: noindex and clean URLs

  • noindex, nofollow, noimageindex and nosnippet, in bulk by content type and taxonomy or one by one.
  • Rules for search results, 404, date, paginated, attachment and author archives, and for RSS feeds.
  • Keep part of a page out of Google’s snippets with data-nosnippet, from the block editor or the classic editor.
  • Remove the base of any taxonomy, drop the parent terms from category URLs, choose a WooCommerce product URL structure and redirect attachment pages to their parent, with 301 redirects from the old URLs.
  • Quick Edit, bulk actions and a Visibility column on your post and term lists.

Sitemaps: control of the native XML sitemap

  • Works on the sitemap WordPress already generates, instead of adding a second one.
  • Exclude post types, taxonomies, users, posts and terms. Noindexed content stays out automatically, and so does content whose canonical URL points to another address.
  • Add URLs of pages served outside WordPress.
  • lastmod dates, and 301 redirects from the sitemap URLs of your previous SEO plugin.
  • Keeps /wp-sitemap.xml answering 200 on a site with no blog posts, which older WordPress versions got wrong.

Redirects: 301, 302, 307 and 410

  • Managed from the admin: no .htaccess editing, no custom table, no 404 log.
  • CSV import and export.
  • A suggested redirect when you delete a post.
  • Take over the redirects WordPress creates when a slug changes.
  • Redirect chains answered in one hop, and loops refused.

Good to know

  • Per-post controls live in the Visibility box below the content, in the block editor and in the classic editor, with a live preview of your Google result, your social card and an AI answer.
  • The Tools tab groups the importers and exports your configuration as JSON for another site.
  • AI agents can audit and edit the SEO of your site through the WordPress Abilities API, with the WordPress MCP Adapter, Novamira or any other client: an SEO inventory, why an address is or is not indexed, the text of entries, the SEO of many entries at once, redirects and noindex rules. EMCP Tools exposes the same fields over MCP while you edit a page in Elementor.
  • Multilingual: works with WPML and Polylang, with a folder or a domain per language.
  • Visibility replaces a full SEO plugin instead of running next to one, and warns you if another one is active.

Perfect companions

Visibility works on its own. These plugins pair well with it:

  • VigIA: see which AI crawlers visit your site. Both plugins share the Site Identity schema without duplicating it.
  • Share Buttons & AI-powered Summaries: share buttons for social networks and AI assistants.
  • AI Content Signals: tell AI systems how they may use your content (training, search or both) through robots.txt.
  • Vigilante: all-in-one WordPress security: firewall, login protection, security headers, 2FA and file integrity monitoring.

External services

This plugin connects to Gravatar (operated by Automattic Inc.) to check whether an author has a public avatar, so it can be used in Open Graph (og:image) and in Person schema (image).

  • What is sent: an MD5 hash of the author email, in a HEAD request to https://www.gravatar.com/avatar/{hash}?d=404. The email address itself is never sent.
  • When: on a single post or page with Open Graph on and no other image available (social image, featured image, WooCommerce gallery image or image in the content), and on an author archive with Person schema on.
  • How often: the result is cached for 24 hours, so later page loads do not contact Gravatar again.

It is the same lookup WordPress uses for comment avatars. Gravatar’s privacy policy: https://automattic.com/privacy/

Performance and security

“Lightweight” should be a measurement, not a slogan. These are the real numbers for this release, refreshed on every update.

Footprint (3.0.0)

  • Download size: about 690 KB zipped.
  • Codebase: 51 PHP files, roughly 39,700 lines of PHP, plus 3,400 lines of JavaScript and 2,600 of CSS, loaded only where they are used.
  • On a page view: 26 PHP files, and no database query added to a post, a page or the home page of a default install.
  • No custom database tables. One option for the settings and native WordPress meta for per-post, per-term and per-author values.
  • No cron jobs.
  • No external HTTP calls, except the cached Gravatar check described above.
  • Built on WordPress core APIs (wp_robots, wp_sitemaps_*, register_post_meta, get_canonical_url, the Block Editor).

Measured against other SEO plugins

The same clean WordPress, the same theme and the same 30 posts, with one SEO plugin active at a time on its default settings. Each figure is what that plugin adds to WordPress with no SEO plugin. Measured in October 2026 on the current release of each one, on a single machine: what carries over to your site is the order, not the exact figure.

  • PHP files loaded on every page view: 26. SureRank 122, SEOPress 134, Rank Math 267, All in One SEO 303, Yoast SEO 588.
  • Database queries added to a post: none. SEOPress 1, Yoast SEO 3, SureRank 7, Rank Math 16, All in One SEO 32.
  • Server time added to every page view: about 2 ms. Yoast SEO 7, SEOPress 8, Rank Math 11, SureRank 12, All in One SEO 17.
  • JavaScript loaded in the editor: 41 KB. SEOPress 89 KB, Rank Math 1.4 MB, SureRank 1.9 MB, Yoast SEO 3.5 MB.
  • Download size: about 690 KB. SEOPress 2.8 MB, Rank Math 3.6 MB, Yoast SEO 4.9 MB, SureRank 6 MB, All in One SEO 7.3 MB.
  • Custom database tables and cron jobs: none. SureRank 0 and 1, SEOPress 1 and 0, Rank Math 6 and 4, Yoast SEO 6 and 6, All in One SEO 13 and 1.

Security

  • Every release passes a security audit of the changed code before it ships.
  • Small attack surface: no custom tables, no unauthenticated endpoints, escaped output, validated input and prepared database queries.
  • No telemetry and no data collection.

Support

Need private support or custom development?

Do you need one-on-one help, priority troubleshooting, or a custom feature, integration, or tweak built specifically for your site? I offer private support and custom development. Just contact me and tell me what you need.

Need help or have suggestions?

  • Official website
  • WordPress support forum
  • YouTube channel
  • Documentation and tutorials

Love the plugin? Please leave us a 5-star review and help spread the word!

About AyudaWP

We are specialists in WordPress security, SEO, AI and performance optimization plugins. We create tools that solve real problems for WordPress site owners while maintaining the highest coding standards and accessibility requirements.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the native-aeo-pack folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install through the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open Visibility in the admin sidebar to review the active modules and tune the defaults.
  4. Done. Meta tags, robots directives and sitemap filters are applied automatically based on your settings.
sections.faq:
Is Visibility an alternative to Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO or SEOPress?

For most sites, yes. It covers titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, Open Graph, schema, robots rules, redirects and the sitemap, and it imports your data from those plugins in one click.

It has no keyword analysis or content scoring. If you need those, keep your current plugin: Visibility is not meant to run alongside another SEO plugin.

How do I migrate from another SEO plugin?

  1. Install and activate Visibility. Your old plugin can be active or already deactivated.
  2. Open the Tools tab. The import card shows what it found, field by field.
  3. Import, check a few entries and deactivate the old plugin.

What to expect:

  • From: Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, The SEO Framework, Slim SEO and SureRank.
  • What comes over: titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs and robots rules of posts and terms, social titles, descriptions and images, schema types, verification codes and title templates.
  • Site identity: entity type (with its organization or business type), name, logo, social profiles, contact, address and company details from SEOPress, Rank Math and Yoast SEO. Coordinates, price range and opening hours from Rank Math.
  • More than one plugin: the one in use takes each value (active first, then installed, then the one set up last), and it decides the entity type.
  • Redirects: from Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress and the Redirection plugin.
  • Templates: variables such as %%title%% are converted. One that needs a custom field or a date is left where it is.
  • Schema of each entry: its type from Yoast SEO, and what it is about from Rank Math, ThinkRank and Schema & Structured Data for WP. The rest of that schema (a second one, a type Visibility does not have, or JSON-LD typed by hand) comes in as read-only JSON-LD, which you can remove in the Schema tab. All in One SEO, SEOPress and SureRank keep it only in their paid versions, which are not imported.
  • Safe to repeat: nothing is deleted from the old plugin, what you already set in Visibility is kept, and running it again never duplicates anything.

I used Native SEO Meta Tags, NoIndexer or Sitemap Customizer. How do I migrate?

Install and activate Visibility, open the Tools tab and click Import now. The import copies your data and never deletes it, and what you already set in Visibility is kept. Then deactivate the old plugins.

Is Visibility free? Is there a Pro version?

It is free. There is no Pro version, no add-ons and no upsell banners. Everything on this page is in the plugin you download, including the redirects, the importers, the WooCommerce URL structures and the AI discovery files. No account and no license key.

Will Visibility slow down my site?

It is built not to: no database tables of its own, no cron jobs and no external calls apart from a cached Gravatar check. Most of the work is done by WordPress core functions. The numbers of each release are in “Performance and security”.

Does Visibility track me or send my data anywhere?

No. There is no telemetry, no usage analytics and no account. The only outside request it can make is the cached Gravatar check described in “External services”, which sends a hash of the author email and never the address.

Are there any database tables?

No. Settings live in one WordPress option, and per-post, per-term and per-user values in native WordPress meta. Deleting the plugin removes the option and keeps those values, so reinstalling does not lose your work.

Can I disable individual modules?

Yes. The Overview tab switches Discover, Indexing, Sitemaps and Redirects on and off independently.

What are AEO and GEO, and does Visibility do them?

AEO (answer engine optimization) and GEO (generative engine optimization) mean being found, understood and cited by AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Google’s AI answers.

Nobody outside those companies knows exactly how they choose their sources, so Visibility works on what you can check yourself:

  • Freshness: a filter and a Last updated column for content that has gone stale.
  • Authorship: author details in Person schema and on the page.
  • Questions and answers: FAQPage from the Q&A you have published.

No plugin can promise you a citation.

How does Visibility help with AI (AEO / GEO)?

It gives AI search and assistants clean signals to read:

  • Site Identity schema: who is behind the site.
  • llms.txt and llms-full.txt: a Markdown index of your content.
  • A Markdown version of every page at its .md URL.
  • A robots.txt editor to allow or block AI crawlers by name.

The companion plugin VigIA shows which AI crawlers actually visit.

Can an AI agent manage my SEO? Does Visibility work with MCP and Novamira?

Yes, on WordPress 6.9 or later, which is where the Abilities API arrived. Visibility registers sixteen abilities with it, and any client finds them: the WordPress MCP Adapter, Novamira and others.

  • Read and write the SEO of a post, a page or a product, one at a time or up to 50 at once.
  • Read and write what an entry is about, with the fields its type takes and the JSON-LD the page will write.
  • Read and write the SEO of a category, a tag or a term.
  • An SEO inventory with filters and warnings, for audits, exports and weekly reports.
  • Why an address is or is not indexed, for a list of URLs, a category or a content type.
  • Find entries by address, title or slug, and read their text.
  • Redirects: the suggested ones, create in bulk, delete.
  • Noindex rules by content type, taxonomy and archive, simulated before they apply.
  • The SEO status of the site.

An agent can do no more than the user it is signed in as: each ability asks for the same permission as the editor or the settings screen. Text that is not open to everyone is never handed over. Visibility adds no server, endpoint or API key of its own.

To switch them off, untick the box in Visibility > Overview > AI agents.

Can I manage the SEO of my posts and products with the REST API?

Yes, with an application password of a user who can edit them:

  • Abilities, the recommended way (see the question above): POST /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities/native-aeo-pack/update-posts-seo/run writes up to 50 entries per call, checks each one on its own and clears the cached page.
  • WordPress REST API: the meta field of /wp/v2/<type>/<id>, with keys such as _native_aeo_pack_title and _native_aeo_pack_description. The REST schema describes each one.
  • WooCommerce REST API: the same keys in the meta_data of /wc/v3/products/<id>.

The social image is the ID of an image in the media library, not a URL.

Does Visibility generate llms.txt and a Markdown version of my pages?

Yes, both, generated on the fly from your content, so there is nothing to regenerate when you publish:

  • /llms.txt: a Markdown index of your site, by content type and taxonomy, with WooCommerce-aware entries.
  • /llms-full.txt: the long version.
  • Every entry also answers at its own .md URL.

Both files are kept in wp-content/uploads/native-aeo-pack/, one per language, and rebuilt on the first request after a change. With the physical file option on, your server has to pass /llms.txt to WordPress when the file is missing.

Keep expectations realistic: llms.txt is a proposed convention, not a standard. Google has said it ignores it and no major AI vendor has confirmed support.

Does Visibility add schema markup and structured data?

Yes, as a single JSON-LD graph, with per-post and per-term overrides:

  • Article, with the type chosen per content type (BlogPosting, NewsArticle and others), or a page type such as FAQPage or QAPage.
  • What each entry is about: a local business (yours or one you review), a person, a service, a product, an event, a software app, a course, a job posting, a recipe, a book, a film, music, a podcast episode, a video, a dataset, a fact check, a forum thread or a how-to.
  • BreadcrumbList.
  • Person and ProfilePage for authors.
  • FAQPage from Details and Accordion blocks.
  • WebSite on the home page, with the site name.
  • Site Identity (Organization, LocalBusiness or Person).

On WooCommerce products, WooCommerce writes the Product and Visibility adds nothing about them.

How do I add a recipe, an event or a product to an entry?

Open the Schema tab of the Visibility box and pick what the entry is about. Its fields are the ones Google reads for that type:

  • The required ones are marked, and the tab says what is still missing.
  • A field left empty follows the template of its content type, set in Discover: the entry title or date, the Site Identity, a custom field or a fixed value.
  • The JSON-LD the page will write is shown as you type.
  • Six types take a review: rating, scale and who signs it.

Nothing is written until the required fields are filled, and nothing on entries that are private, password-protected or for members only.

Does Visibility add local business (local SEO) schema?

Yes. In Discover > Site Identity pick Local business as the entity type:

  • Business type: Restaurant, Dentist, Store and many more, or the generic LocalBusiness.
  • Address and coordinates.
  • Phone and email.
  • Price range.
  • Opening hours, with split hours.
  • Cuisine and menu, for restaurants, cafés, bars and other food businesses.

Google lists the address as required for a local business. The settings screen warns you when it is missing.

It is one node on the home page, shared with the rest of the schema. With several premises, give each one its page and pick Local business: a location of yours in its Schema tab: each one is linked to the Site Identity as its parent organization. To review a business that is not yours, pick Local business: one this entry reviews.

My business has more than one location. Can I mark up the others?

Visibility describes one business. Give each other location a page of its own and add its node there with the native_aeo_pack_schema_graph filter:

add_filter( 'native_aeo_pack_schema_graph', function ( $graph, $context, $post ) {
    if ( 'article' === $context && $post && 'riverside' === $post->post_name ) {
        $graph[] = array(
            '@type'              => 'Restaurant',
            '@id'                => get_permalink( $post ) . '#business',
            'name'               => 'Casa Marta Riverside',
            'url'                => get_permalink( $post ),
            'address'            => array(
                '@type'           => 'PostalAddress',
                'streetAddress'   => 'Calle del Río, 3',
                'addressLocality' => 'Segovia',
                'addressCountry'  => 'ES',
            ),
            'parentOrganization' => array( '@id' => home_url( '/#identity' ) ),
        );
    }
    return $graph;
}, 10, 3 );

Google asks for each location to be a LocalBusiness of its own, with the address of its page in url.

How do I tell Google the name of my site?

In Discover > Site name:

  • Site name: empty, it is the name of the organization or business in Site Identity, or the site title.
  • Alternate names: an acronym or a shorter name, one per line.

They go in the WebSite markup of the home page, which is where Google reads the site name from, and in og:site_name. The WebSite is written with Site Identity off too.

Google decides which name to show. Keep the site title, or the title of your home page, consistent with it.

The Rich Results Test does not show my organization. Why?

The test only lists an organization that carries a contact detail. Add an email or a phone in Discover > Site Identity and it shows up.

Without one, the markup is still valid and Google still reads the name, the logo and the profiles. You can see it in the page source or in validator.schema.org.

Can I stop Visibility from writing schema and use a specialised plugin instead?

Yes, at three levels:

  • Everything: uncheck JSON-LD: Article and BreadcrumbList in the Discover tab.
  • One content type: set its schema type to None.
  • One entry: pick None in its Schema type field.

None adds no Article, BreadcrumbList or FAQPage to that content. Site Identity is a separate setting and keeps working. Developers can also use the native_aeo_pack_schema_graph filter.

Does Visibility mark up author pages as ProfilePage?

Yes. The author archive of anyone with at least one published post gets a ProfilePage with their Person: job title, topics, credentials and profiles.

An author can also pick a page, such as About me, as their profile page, and that page becomes their ProfilePage. The Author details block or the [visibility_author_details] shortcode shows those fields on the page, or Author details on profile pages, in Discover, adds them at the end of it.

An author is anyone who can write posts or pages, or has a published post.

How do I change how the Author details look?

Visibility adds no styles, so each theme shows them its own way. The markup is the same in the block, the shortcode and the automatic details: a list with the class wp-block-native-aeo-pack-author-details, a dt for each section (Job title, Topics, Credentials, Profiles) and a dd for each value.

  • The block: set its colors, font size, line height and spacing in the editor.
  • Anywhere: add CSS in Appearance > Customize > Additional CSS or, with a block theme, in Appearance > Editor > Styles > Additional CSS.

This example puts each section on one line, as in “Topics: WordPress · WooCommerce”:

.wp-block-native-aeo-pack-author-details dt,
.wp-block-native-aeo-pack-author-details dd {
    display: inline;
    margin: 0;
}
.wp-block-native-aeo-pack-author-details dt {
    font-weight: 600;
}
.wp-block-native-aeo-pack-author-details dt:not(:first-child)::before {
    content: "\A";
    white-space: pre;
}
.wp-block-native-aeo-pack-author-details dt::after {
    content: ":\00a0";
    content: ":\00a0" / "";
}
.wp-block-native-aeo-pack-author-details dd + dd::before {
    content: "\00a0· ";
    content: "\00a0· " / "";
}

The \00a0 keeps a label with its first value and the dot at the end of a line. The second content hides the colon and the dot from screen readers, and browsers that do not know it keep the first.

To style them only on the author archive, put body.author before each selector.

Does Visibility control the XML sitemap?

Yes. It customizes the sitemap WordPress already generates at /wp-sitemap.xml, so there is no second sitemap, no cache to clear and nothing to rebuild:

  • Exclude post types, taxonomies, single posts and terms, and users by role.
  • Noindexed content stays out automatically.
  • Content whose Canonical URL points to another address stays out too. Google asks not to list one address in the sitemap and declare another as canonical.
  • Add URLs of pages that are not WordPress content.
  • Set lastmod dates and the number of URLs per sitemap.
  • The sitemap URLs of your previous SEO plugin (sitemap.xml, post-sitemap.xml) are 301-redirected to the native one.

My sitemap looks fine in the browser but Google says it could not be read. Why?

Because it answers with a 404 status while showing the right file, and Google discards any sitemap that does not answer 200. It happens on sites with no published blog posts: a shop, a portfolio, a site made of pages only.

Whether it affects you depends on your WordPress version: it was fixed in WordPress 7.1.1, from a report that came out of this plugin. On older versions, Visibility answers /wp-sitemap.xml with a 200 itself, with a switch for it in the Sitemaps tab. A sitemap with nothing in it still answers 404, as it should.

My old sitemap URLs redirect to a page that does not exist. What is wrong?

Something has switched off the sitemap WordPress generates, so the old address has nowhere to go. The usual causes:

  • A snippet that sets wp_sitemaps_enabled to false, in functions.php or in a snippets plugin.
  • Another SEO plugin serving a sitemap of its own.
  • “Discourage search engines from indexing this site” ticked in Settings > Reading.

Visibility checks before redirecting and leaves the old address alone in that case.

Does Visibility manage redirects? Do I need .htaccess or a separate plugin?

Redirects are included and you need neither:

  • 301, 302, 307 and 410, with no .htaccess editing and no custom table.
  • CSV import and export.
  • A suggested redirect when you delete a post.
  • Take over or remove the redirects WordPress creates when a slug changes.
  • A redirect whose target is redirected too is answered in one hop, and one that would close a loop is refused.
  • A target that is the old address of an entry is flagged, with a button to answer it in one hop.
  • Targets get the trailing slash of your permalinks, before any ? or #.
  • Every redirect says X-Redirect-By: Visibility.

It does not log 404 errors, on purpose: that needs a table and a cleanup job. The companion plugin VigIA records the 404s that crawlers hit.

Does Visibility work with the AI plugin of WordPress.org?

Yes. Its Meta Description Generation experiment saves the description it writes in the Meta description field of Visibility, so the page prints one meta description and not two. The descriptions it was printing on its own are copied to that field by the update that brings this in, where the field is empty.

Does Visibility work with Elementor, Divi and other page builders?

Yes. The Visibility box shows below the content, in the block editor and on the classic editing screen a builder uses when it replaces the block editor.

With Elementor, the Markdown version of a page is built from the Elementor layout, so AI agents get the real text. With Divi, Avada, WPBakery and other builders that keep the text in shortcodes or in blocks of their own, llms-full.txt carries it too.

Does Visibility work with WooCommerce?

Yes:

  • Products, categories, tags and attributes get titles, descriptions, social tags, schema and robots rules like any other content.
  • The product gallery image is a fallback for og:image.
  • llms.txt is WooCommerce-aware.
  • Cleaner product and category URLs: see “Can I clean up my WooCommerce URLs?”.

It does not add Product schema: WooCommerce already does, with price, stock and reviews.

Does it work with custom post types and custom taxonomies?

Yes, with all public post types and taxonomies. WooCommerce attributes need “Enable Archives?” switched on in their settings.

Can I preview how my page will look on Google, social networks and AI answers?

Yes. The Visibility box has a live preview with three views: your Google result, your social card and an AI Overview citing your page. It updates as you type.

It shows what goes into your HTML, not a score: the final look depends on each platform.

Can I change how the automatic title tag is composed?

Yes, with a template in the Discover tab. Combine these placeholders with your own words:

  • %%title%%: the title of the page.
  • %%sep%%: the separator you chose.
  • %%sitename%% and %%tagline%%.
  • %%page%%: the page number.
  • %%taxonomy%%: the first category of the entry, or the product category of a product.

Example: %%title%% %%sep%% %%sitename%%.

  • The front page, each content type and each taxonomy can have a template of their own.
  • A Meta title typed on an entry or a term always wins.
  • The meta description works the same way, with one more placeholder: %%excerpt%%.
  • Custom fields and dates are not available, on purpose: they need a query on every page.
  • A theme that prints its own title tag, without the WordPress title API, is not reached by the template.

How do I set noindex on a single post?

Open the Visibility box below the content and tick noindex. In the block editor, the eye button in the top bar shows and hides it.

You can also use Quick Edit or Bulk Actions in the post list, and in the category, tag and taxonomy lists.

How do I keep part of a page out of Google’s snippets?

  • Block editor: turn on Keep out of search snippets in the Advanced panel of a Group block, or apply the format of the same name to selected words.
  • Classic editor: use the button of the same name in the Visual toolbar, or nosnippet in the Text tab.

Visibility also leaves that text out of the descriptions and summaries it generates. The Markdown version and llms-full.txt keep the whole page.

The mark on a Group stops applying if you deactivate Visibility. The one on words stays in the content.

What does Respect nosnippet do?

nosnippet tells Google to show no snippet and not to use the text in AI Overviews and AI Mode. Respect nosnippet (Discover tab) applies the same to the files Visibility generates. With it on, an entry set to nosnippet:

  • is listed in llms.txt by title and link only,
  • has no text in llms-full.txt,
  • has no Markdown version,
  • gets no FAQPage.

It is on in new installs. On an update it turns on only if that changes nothing your site already serves.

Does my robots.txt always work, even on a subdirectory install?

Yes. WordPress alone can answer 404 at /robots.txt on a subdirectory install or when its rewrite rules are stale. Visibility serves /robots.txt itself, so it always loads.

If another plugin writes a physical robots.txt, Visibility adds its rules to that file in a block of its own and leaves the rest untouched. /?robots=1 is redirected to /robots.txt.

Does Visibility work on WordPress Multisite?

Yes, and each site keeps its own settings:

  • On a subdomain or mapped-domain network, each site serves its own /robots.txt and /llms.txt.
  • On a subdirectory network there is one robots.txt at the domain root, owned by the main site.
  • A physical file is written only where it belongs: a single site, or the main site of a subdirectory network.
  • Is a physical robots.txt in the network root giving every site the same rules? On Apache and LiteSpeed, a button in the Discover tab routes /robots.txt through WordPress. Only a network administrator sees it.
  • On nginx, the screen gives you the directive for whoever administers the server.

Activate Visibility per site or for the whole network.

Does Visibility work with WPML and Polylang?

Yes, with a folder or a domain per language, and it is listed as compatible in the WPML plugin directory. Visibility ships a wpml-config.xml, which Polylang reads too:

  • The Meta title, Meta description and social title and description of each entry are translated with the entry.
  • Robots, sitemap and llms.txt choices are the same in every language: set one on any translation and it applies to all of them. The Canonical URL is not shared, so each translation keeps its own address.
  • With WPML, choices that already differ between languages stay as they are until you change one. Polylang makes them equal whenever an entry is saved.
  • Title templates, the home page description and the Site Identity texts are translated in WPML > String Translation or Polylang > Languages > Translations. Save the Visibility settings once so they show up there.
  • The site description in llms.txt and in the schema is the Site Identity description or, if that is empty, the WordPress tagline. Translate the one you use.
  • Categories and tags: fill in their SEO fields on each translation.
  • Each language gets its own og:locale, llms.txt, llms-full.txt and Markdown versions.
  • A redirect applies to the exact path written in it. With a folder per language, add one per language (/old-page and /en/old-page).

My site has one domain per language. Anything to know?

  • A redirect holds for every domain, because it matches a path. A relative target (/new-page/) goes to the domain asked for. It cannot send the same old path to a different page in each language.
  • Leave Site Identity > URL empty: each domain then uses its own.
  • Use the virtual llms.txt and robots.txt. A physical file in the site root is the same for every domain, so it lists the addresses of one of them.
  • A physical .txt file with broken accents is sent by your server without a charset: set UTF-8 for .txt files in the server, or use the virtual files, which Visibility always sends as UTF-8.

Does the sitemap include every language?

  • WPML with a folder per language: the sitemap of the default language lists the sub-sitemaps of every language, so the one in robots.txt covers them all.
  • Polylang does the same itself. Exclusions, noindex and lastmod work in each language.
  • One domain per language: each domain has its own sitemap and robots.txt. Submit each one in Search Console.
  • There is no hreflang in the sitemap. WPML and Polylang add it to every page, and Google needs only one method.

Where does Visibility store per-post overrides?

In standard WordPress post meta (_native_aeo_pack_* keys). Term overrides go to term meta and author fields to user meta.

Can I copy my configuration to another site?

Yes. The Tools tab exports your settings and the per-entry and per-term values as one JSON file, and imports it on another site.

  • Content is matched by slug, so it works between sites that are not clones.
  • On import, choose between filling in only what is empty (the default) and replacing what is there.
  • Nothing is created: values land on content that already exists.
  • Redirects have their own CSV export in the Redirects tab. Author profile fields are not included.

How do I know which content has gone stale?

Set a threshold in the Discover tab (90 days by default). Your content lists get a “Not updated in 90 days” filter with a count, and a sortable Last updated column. Set it to 0 to switch both off.

Why it matters: an Ahrefs analysis of 17 million citations found that the pages AI assistants cite were updated more recently, on average, than the ones ranking in Google’s organic results. Google’s AI Overviews were the exception.

Can I clean up my WooCommerce URLs?

Yes, in the Indexing tab:

  • Remove the base of each taxonomy on its own: /product-category/, /product-tag/, /brand/.
  • Drop the parent categories from category URLs, taxonomy by taxonomy (/sweater/ instead of /clothing/sweater/), as Premmerce Permalink Manager and Rank Math do.
  • Choose a product URL structure WooCommerce does not allow: the product slug alone (/my-product/), the category and the slug (/t-shirts/my-product/) or the full category path.
  • Old URLs are 301-redirected to the new ones, so a product is never reachable at two URLs.

Good to know:

  • A page or a term that already uses a path keeps it.
  • Removing a base adds rewrite rules for every term. The settings screen tells you how many before you save.
  • If you use Premmerce Permalink Manager, import its structure from the Tools tab (everything except the URL ending, such as .html), check your URLs and deactivate it.

Does Visibility generate FAQ structured data?

Yes, from content you already have. Switch on JSON-LD: FAQPage in the Discover tab and Visibility reads the Details and Accordion blocks of your entries: the question from the heading, the answer from the content.

It is off by default, because a Details block is not always a question. It helps AI assistants read your Q&A. It does not bring back Google’s FAQ rich results, which Google no longer shows.

Is there an API for plugins and themes?

Yes.

Read what Visibility resolved:

  • Native_AEO_Pack_Frontend_Robots::is_noindex( $post_id ), is_nofollow( $post_id ), is_term_noindex( $term_id, $taxonomy ) and is_term_nofollow( $term_id, $taxonomy ).
  • Native_AEO_Pack_Settings::get( $group, $key, $default ).
  • Native_AEO_Pack_Settings::is_robots_ai_blocking() and get_robots_ai_agents().

Change what is printed, with eight filters:

  • native_aeo_pack_schema_graph ($graph, $context, $object): the JSON-LD nodes before they are printed. $context is article, person, identity or website (the WebSite node on its own, on the home page of a site that prints its identity on another page or has it off). Return an empty array to print nothing.
  • native_aeo_pack_identity_business_types ($types): the schema.org types offered for a local business identity.
  • native_aeo_pack_identity_food_types ($types): the business types that take a cuisine and a menu.
  • native_aeo_pack_document_title ($title): the Meta title before it reaches <title>. Return plain text, which is escaped afterwards, or an empty string to hand the title back to the theme.
  • native_aeo_pack_canonical_url ($url, $object): the canonical of a listing. Return an empty string to print none. Single entries keep the core get_canonical_url filter.
  • native_aeo_pack_meta_description ($description): the final description, used in the meta tag, Open Graph, the Twitter card and the schema.
  • native_aeo_pack_og_image ($image, $post): the image chosen for a single entry.
  • native_aeo_pack_schema_faq_pairs ($pairs, $post): the question and answer pairs before they become FAQPage. Return an empty array to skip it.

React to what an AI agent changed through the abilities, with these actions:

  • native_aeo_pack_post_seo_updated ($post_id): after the SEO values of an entry changed.
  • native_aeo_pack_term_seo_updated ($term_id, $taxonomy): after the SEO values of a term changed.
  • native_aeo_pack_indexing_rules_updated ($changes): after the indexing rules of the site changed.
  • native_aeo_pack_purge_urls ($urls): after some addresses changed what they show, for a page cache Visibility does not purge on its own.
  • native_aeo_pack_purge_all: the same, for a change that reaches every page.
sections.changelog:
3.4.1

Clearer help texts, template tags as buttons, sponsored and ugc links in both editors, 55 AI crawlers to block, slug redirects moved to Visibility in bulk, and fixes for WPML and for plugins switched off for a while.

  • Improved: Help texts rewritten so each one says first what happens, at about half the length. Technical terms appear as code, and the buttons, tabs and settings they name go in quotes, so translations can name them properly.
  • Improved: Template tags such as %%title%% and %%sep%% appear as a row of buttons under each field that takes them, like the available tags of the Permalinks screen. Hover a button to see what it adds. Under the fields per content type and per taxonomy, the row shows when you click into the field.
  • Improved: The front page description override offers its template tags too, with %%tagline%%, what it uses when empty, as placeholder.
  • Improved: The notice shown while WordPress has its sitemap switched off says that nothing on the Sitemaps tab applies until it is back on.
  • Improved: Links can be marked as sponsored or ugc. In the classic editor, two checkboxes sit next to “Mark as nofollow”. In the block editor, a button next to the link button sets them, and they stay when the link is edited again. Each one adds or removes only its own rel value.
  • Improved: The sitemap icon of the entry and term lists says why one is out of the sitemap: ticked by hand, set to noindex, its content type or taxonomy left out, its ID or slug on the “Sitemaps” tab, or a canonical URL that is another address.
  • Improved: On the “Redirects” tab, the redirects WordPress keeps when a slug changes can be moved to Visibility in bulk, or one by one with “Move to Visibility”, to edit them as your own. The “Create 301…” and “Create 410” buttons of the suggestions say what they do on hover.
  • Improved: The AI crawlers you can block in robots.txt go from 18 to 55: the training crawlers Google lists in its own robots.txt, and the search and on-request crawlers of Anthropic, Mistral, Kimi, SB Intuitions and Exa. If you had every training crawler ticked, the new training ones are ticked on update; any other selection stays as it was, and no search crawler is ever ticked for you. Each group shows how many are ticked, with “Select all” and “Deselect all”, and folds its list.
  • Improved: The ability that finds content with no Meta title or description lists it without loading the custom fields of every entry, which weighed most on sites built with page builders.
  • Fix: The AIOSEO importer brings over “Remove Category Base Prefix”, so /category/ no longer comes back in category addresses after migrating.
  • Fix: Schema texts typed in an entry keep sequences such as %C3%A9 or 100%AB, which were deleted on save.
  • Fix: The Home category for apps shared its translation with the Home breadcrumb, so in some languages it showed the wrong word.
  • Fix: With WPML, the bulk actions of the entries list, such as “Set as nofollow”, copied both values of the directive to the translations and overwrote a translation’s own exclusion from the per-type rule. They copy only the value they change, once per group of translations.
  • Fix: A content type or taxonomy that is not registered at that moment, because a plugin such as WooCommerce is switched off for a while, no longer drops out of the settings on save or import: the per-type directives, llms.txt, Markdown, the sitemap exclusions, the title and description templates and the schema type.
  • Fix: Moving to Visibility a WordPress slug redirect whose old address has accents could replace a Visibility redirect already set for that address, such as a 410.

3.4.0

Ten new abilities for AI agents: an SEO inventory, why an address is or is not indexed, finding entries and reading their text, writing many at once, redirects and noindex rules. Page caches are purged after every change.

  • New: An SEO inventory for AI agents, with each entry’s resolved title, description, canonical, indexability, sitemap and schema, filters and warnings already worked out (length, duplicates, noindex in the sitemap).
  • New: An ability that explains whether a list of addresses, a category or a content type is indexable, why not, and what does not add up.
  • New: Abilities to find entries by address, title or slug, and to read their text as Markdown. What is not open to everyone is never handed over.
  • New: An ability that writes the SEO of up to 50 entries in one call, each one checked on its own.
  • New: Redirects for AI agents: the suggested ones, creating them in bulk without hiding a live page or closing a loop, and deleting them.
  • New: Noindex rules by content type, taxonomy and special archive for AI agents, simulated first with the number of entries they change.
  • Improved: After an ability changes the SEO of an entry or a term, the page caches of DietPress, SiteGround Optimizer, WP Super Cache, LiteSpeed Cache, WP Rocket and W3 Total Cache drop that page.
  • Improved: The custom fields of Visibility describe themselves in the REST schema, for agents that write custom fields directly.

For older changelog entries, please check the changelog.txt file

short_description: Lightweight Free WordPress SEO: meta tags, schema, Open Graph, redirects, robots, LLMS, MD, sitemap. No bloat, no tracking. Visible to search and AI.
description:
Visibility is the SEO essentials in one light plugin: meta tags, canonical URLs, Open Graph, schema, robots rules, redirects, a robots.txt editor, llms.txt, Markdown for AI agents and control of the native XML sitemap, in about 690 KB.

  • Free, all of it. No Pro version, no upsell banners, no account.
  • No tracking. Nothing phones home.
  • Light. Built on WordPress core APIs, with no database tables of its own and no cron jobs.
  • Easy to switch to. One-click import from Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, The SEO Framework, Slim SEO and SureRank.
  • Ready for AI search (AEO and GEO). Clean metadata, llms.txt and a Markdown version of every page, for ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and other AI assistants to read and cite.

Four modules, switch on only what you need

Discover: meta tags, schema and AI discovery

  • Meta title and meta description, with templates and per-post and per-term overrides.
  • Canonical URLs on entries and on every listing.
  • Open Graph and Twitter Cards.
  • JSON-LD schema: Article, BreadcrumbList, Person, ProfilePage, FAQPage and Site Identity (Organization, LocalBusiness or Person). Choose the type per content type, or None to leave it to another plugin.
  • What each entry is about, in its own Schema tab: a local business, a product, a service, an event, a recipe, a book, a course, a job posting, a how-to and ten more types, with an optional review. A template per content type fills it from the entry, a custom field or the Site Identity, and it is written only with what Google requires.
  • Author details (job title, topics and credentials), shown with the Author details block or the [visibility_author_details] shortcode. Each author can pick a page as their profile page.
  • AI discovery: llms.txt, llms-full.txt, a Markdown version of each page and a robots.txt editor with AI crawler rules.
  • Respect nosnippet: content set to nosnippet stays out of the llms.txt summaries, llms-full.txt, Markdown and FAQPage.
  • A filter for content that has not been updated in a while.

Indexing: noindex and clean URLs

  • noindex, nofollow, noimageindex and nosnippet, in bulk by content type and taxonomy or one by one.
  • Rules for search results, 404, date, paginated, attachment and author archives, and for RSS feeds.
  • Keep part of a page out of Google’s snippets with data-nosnippet, from the block editor or the classic editor.
  • Remove the base of any taxonomy, drop the parent terms from category URLs, choose a WooCommerce product URL structure and redirect attachment pages to their parent, with 301 redirects from the old URLs.
  • Quick Edit, bulk actions and a Visibility column on your post and term lists.

Sitemaps: control of the native XML sitemap

  • Works on the sitemap WordPress already generates, instead of adding a second one.
  • Exclude post types, taxonomies, users, posts and terms. Noindexed content stays out automatically, and so does content whose canonical URL points to another address.
  • Add URLs of pages served outside WordPress.
  • lastmod dates, and 301 redirects from the sitemap URLs of your previous SEO plugin.
  • Keeps /wp-sitemap.xml answering 200 on a site with no blog posts, which older WordPress versions got wrong.

Redirects: 301, 302, 307 and 410

  • Managed from the admin: no .htaccess editing, no custom table, no 404 log.
  • CSV import and export.
  • A suggested redirect when you delete a post.
  • Take over the redirects WordPress creates when a slug changes.
  • Redirect chains answered in one hop, and loops refused.

Good to know

  • Per-post controls live in the Visibility box below the content, in the block editor and in the classic editor, with a live preview of your Google result, your social card and an AI answer.
  • The Tools tab groups the importers and exports your configuration as JSON for another site.
  • AI agents can audit and edit the SEO of your site through the WordPress Abilities API, with the WordPress MCP Adapter, Novamira or any other client: an SEO inventory, why an address is or is not indexed, the text of entries, the SEO of many entries at once, redirects and noindex rules. EMCP Tools exposes the same fields over MCP while you edit a page in Elementor.
  • Multilingual: works with WPML and Polylang, with a folder or a domain per language.
  • Visibility replaces a full SEO plugin instead of running next to one, and warns you if another one is active.

Perfect companions

Visibility works on its own. These plugins pair well with it:

  • VigIA: see which AI crawlers visit your site. Both plugins share the Site Identity schema without duplicating it.
  • Share Buttons & AI-powered Summaries: share buttons for social networks and AI assistants.
  • AI Content Signals: tell AI systems how they may use your content (training, search or both) through robots.txt.
  • Vigilante: all-in-one WordPress security: firewall, login protection, security headers, 2FA and file integrity monitoring.

External services

This plugin connects to Gravatar (operated by Automattic Inc.) to check whether an author has a public avatar, so it can be used in Open Graph (og:image) and in Person schema (image).

  • What is sent: an MD5 hash of the author email, in a HEAD request to https://www.gravatar.com/avatar/{hash}?d=404. The email address itself is never sent.
  • When: on a single post or page with Open Graph on and no other image available (social image, featured image, WooCommerce gallery image or image in the content), and on an author archive with Person schema on.
  • How often: the result is cached for 24 hours, so later page loads do not contact Gravatar again.

It is the same lookup WordPress uses for comment avatars. Gravatar’s privacy policy: https://automattic.com/privacy/

Performance and security

“Lightweight” should be a measurement, not a slogan. These are the real numbers for this release, refreshed on every update.

Footprint (3.0.0)

  • Download size: about 690 KB zipped.
  • Codebase: 51 PHP files, roughly 39,700 lines of PHP, plus 3,400 lines of JavaScript and 2,600 of CSS, loaded only where they are used.
  • On a page view: 26 PHP files, and no database query added to a post, a page or the home page of a default install.
  • No custom database tables. One option for the settings and native WordPress meta for per-post, per-term and per-author values.
  • No cron jobs.
  • No external HTTP calls, except the cached Gravatar check described above.
  • Built on WordPress core APIs (wp_robots, wp_sitemaps_*, register_post_meta, get_canonical_url, the Block Editor).

Measured against other SEO plugins

The same clean WordPress, the same theme and the same 30 posts, with one SEO plugin active at a time on its default settings. Each figure is what that plugin adds to WordPress with no SEO plugin. Measured in October 2026 on the current release of each one, on a single machine: what carries over to your site is the order, not the exact figure.

  • PHP files loaded on every page view: 26. SureRank 122, SEOPress 134, Rank Math 267, All in One SEO 303, Yoast SEO 588.
  • Database queries added to a post: none. SEOPress 1, Yoast SEO 3, SureRank 7, Rank Math 16, All in One SEO 32.
  • Server time added to every page view: about 2 ms. Yoast SEO 7, SEOPress 8, Rank Math 11, SureRank 12, All in One SEO 17.
  • JavaScript loaded in the editor: 41 KB. SEOPress 89 KB, Rank Math 1.4 MB, SureRank 1.9 MB, Yoast SEO 3.5 MB.
  • Download size: about 690 KB. SEOPress 2.8 MB, Rank Math 3.6 MB, Yoast SEO 4.9 MB, SureRank 6 MB, All in One SEO 7.3 MB.
  • Custom database tables and cron jobs: none. SureRank 0 and 1, SEOPress 1 and 0, Rank Math 6 and 4, Yoast SEO 6 and 6, All in One SEO 13 and 1.

Security

  • Every release passes a security audit of the changed code before it ships.
  • Small attack surface: no custom tables, no unauthenticated endpoints, escaped output, validated input and prepared database queries.
  • No telemetry and no data collection.

Support

Need private support or custom development?

Do you need one-on-one help, priority troubleshooting, or a custom feature, integration, or tweak built specifically for your site? I offer private support and custom development. Just contact me and tell me what you need.

Need help or have suggestions?

  • Official website
  • WordPress support forum
  • YouTube channel
  • Documentation and tutorials

Love the plugin? Please leave us a 5-star review and help spread the word!

About AyudaWP

We are specialists in WordPress security, SEO, AI and performance optimization plugins. We create tools that solve real problems for WordPress site owners while maintaining the highest coding standards and accessibility requirements.
